faqs.a: Code 39 handles letters and digits, so it suits asset tags, IDs, and internal labels. Interleaved 2 of 5 is digits-only but denser, which suits cartons and shipping labels. For retail products sold in stores you need EAN-13 or UPC-A, which this tool does not generate.
Code 39 encodes 43 characters: A-Z, 0-9, space, and - . $ / + %. Lowercase letters are converted to uppercase automatically. Anything outside this set shows a validation error.

Three usual causes: the barcode is too small (keep the narrow bar at least 0.25 mm when printed), there is no quiet zone (this tool adds one automatically), or the contrast is poor (always black on white, never reversed or on a photo background).

barcode-generator.formula:
Code 39: symbol = * + data + * ; each character = 9 elements (5 bars, 4 spaces), exactly 3 wide.
ITF check digit: sum = digits x 3,1,3,1... from the right; check = (10 - sum mod 10) mod 10.

keyFacts: A barcode stores data in the widths of printed bars and spaces. A scanner reads the pattern of wide and narrow elements.
Code 39 encodes 43 characters (A-Z, 0-9, space, - . $ / + %). Each character uses 9 elements: 5 bars and 4 spaces, exactly 3 of them wide.
Every Code 39 symbol starts and ends with *, so the scanner knows the direction and boundaries.
Interleaved 2 of 5 encodes digit pairs: bars carry one digit, spaces carry the next. It needs an even digit count and a mod-10 check digit.
The blank margin on each side is the quiet zone. Scanners need it; this tool adds 10 narrow modules automatically.

barcode-generator.workedExample:
Code 39 for the text A1:
1. Wrap with start/stop: * A 1 * (4 characters).
2. Each character is 9 elements. * = 13 narrow units, A = 15, 1 = 13.
3. Add 3 inter-character gaps: 13 + 1 + 15 + 1 + 13 + 1 + 13 = 57 units.
4. Add the quiet zones (10 units each side): 77 units wide in total.
Interleaved 2 of 5 for 1234:
1. Check digit: 4x3 + 3x1 + 2x3 + 1x1 = 22; (10 - 2) mod 10 = 8, giving 12348.
2. Odd length, so pad: 012348, encoded as pairs (0,1) (2,3) (4,8).
